difficult patients can negatively impact healthcare providers and the healthcare system, and psychologists can play a role in reducing these impacts by: (a) supporting provider wellness; (b) providing relevant education to clinical teams; and (c) improving the quality of patient care.
the definition of a difficult patient varies across clinicians, settings, and systems.
the concept of a difficult patient in healthcare is a complex one, with a number of contributing patient, clinician and systems factors that can influence patient-clinician interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the factors that contribute to difficult patient–clinician encounters, and the role of psychologists in addressing these issues.
how psychologists can contribute to the development of effective, efficient, and compassionate interdisciplinary care for patients with complex needs and their clinicians.
the role of psychologists in the age of interdisciplinary care.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

“difficult patients” are not a homogeneous group of people, but rather a complex interaction between patients, clinicians, and the healthcare environment; psychologists can be a valuable resource to help clinicians understand the etiology of “difficult” patient-clinician encounters; and psychologists can help clinicians improve patient care for difficult clinical patients.

(1) difficult patients are a reality in healthcare; (2) difficult patients are not a problem of the individual patient but a problem of the healthcare system; (3) difficult patients can be a source of stress for clinicians; (4) difficult patients can have a negative impact on patient care; and (5) difficult patients can negatively impact the healthcare system.

difficult patients are a fact of life in healthcare settings; difficult patients are a source of stress for clinicians and patients; difficult patients are not necessarily “difficult” for all clinicians; difficult patients are more likely to occur in certain settings and organizations than others; and, finally, psychologists are in a unique position to help clinicians, patients, and organizations address the problems that difficult patients present.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
difficult patients can be managed effectively, with the help of psychologists and other health professionals, in order to provide high-quality care for all.

difficult patients are not the sole source of difficult patient encounters; rather, difficult patient encounters are the result of a complex interaction of patient, clinicians, and healthcare system factors.

psychologists can play a key role on interprofessional teams by helping to: improve patient care for difficult-to-treat patients; support clinician wellness; provide education and training to other clinical providers; and reduce the stress placed on the healthcare system by difficult patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that

psychologists in medical settings have a unique opportunity to improve the care of difficult patients, support provider wellness, and reduce the stress that difficult patient place on healthcare systems.
psychologists can play a vital role in helping clinicians manage difficult patients.
psychologists can serve as a valuable resource in the management of difficult patients in medical settings.
